results.Peyton: Peyton is an English surname and a unisex given name. In Ireland it is known to have been among the anglicized forms of Ó Peatáin.
results.Reed: Reed  may be either a surname or given name.
results.Rowan: Rowan () is a traditionally masculine Irish given name and surname, now also in use as a given name for girls. Variants of the name include Roan, Rohan, Ruadhán, and Ruadh.
results.Sage: Sage () is a family name and a given name. It can also be spelled Saige or Sayge or Sayje.
results.Seren:
Seren is a given name in Welsh, and both a given name and surname in Turkish. 
In Welsh, it is a female and male name meaning "star".
results.Shelby:
Shelby is a surname and may also be a given name.
The surname's origin is obscure, but may derive from Middle English salwe (“willow, sallow”) + -by (“settlement, farm”).
results.Sheldon: Sheldon is an English surname, as well as a masculine given name, combining the Old English scelf (rock ledge shelf) and the place name haddon, which in turn comes from the words hǣth (heath) and dūn (hill; but also, valley).
results.Shirley: Shirley is a given name and a surname originating from the English place-name Shirley, which is derived from the Old English elements scire ("shire") or scīr ("bright, clear") and lēah ("wood, clearing, meadow, enclosure").
results.Sierra: Sierra is both a surname and a feminine given name. It is the Spanish word for saw or mountain range.
results.Silas: Silas is a common given name and a lesser-known surname. It is a cognate of Silvanus.
results.Skye: Skye is both a given name and surname.
results.Solomon: Solomon is a masculine given name and surname of Hebrew origin, popularized by the biblical figure Solomon, Israelite monarch and son of David. The name is derived from the Latin Solomōn, borrowed from the Ancient Greek Solomṓn (Σολομών), ultimately from the Hebrew Šĕlōmō (שְׁלֹמֹה).
results.Wesley: Wesley is a name with an Anglo-Saxon (Old English) etymology. It is derived from the surname "Westlēah".
results.Wilder: Wilder is an English and German surname, sometimes used as a given name, meaning "untamed" or "wild", a wild, free, or natural state or existence, also passionately eager or enthusiastic.
results.Winston: Winston is a surname derived from Winstone, near Cirencester in Gloucestershire. Later, it developed as a male Christian name with the Churchill family, starting with Sir Winston Churchill in 1620, named for his mother Sarah's surname.
results.Wren:
Wren is both an English surname and a gender neutral given name, both derived from the English name of the songbird.
It has recently increased in popularity as a name for girls and boys in the Anglosphere along with other names derived from the natural world.
results.Zoe: Zoe is a feminine first name of Greek origin, meaning "life."
results.Achim: Achim is a male forename and a surname.
results.Anna: Anna is a feminine given name, the Latin form of the Hebrew name Hannah (Hebrew: חַנָּה, romanized: Ḥannāh), meaning "favour" or "grace". It is the name of Samuel's mother in the Hebrew Bible, rendered Ἄννα in Greek, Hannah in English, and Anna in Latin.
results.Augusta: Augusta can be a given name or surname. It could be derived from Augustae, a title used for the Empresses of the Roman and Byzantine Empires or simply as a feminine variant of August.
results.Christine: Christine is feminine given name of Greek origin. " Variants include: Christina, Kristin, Kristina, Kristine, Kristen, Kirsten, Khrystyna (Ukraine), Krystyna (Poland), Kristiina (Estonia & Finland), and Cristina (Italy, Spain, Portugal, Central & South America).
results.Cornelius: Cornelius is an originally Roman masculine name. Its derivation is uncertain but is suspected to be from the Latin cornu, "horn".
results.Dirk: Dirk is a male given name of Dutch origin. It is a traditional diminutive of the Dutch name Diederik.
results.Ella: Ella is a personal name most often used as a feminine given name, but also as a surname, especially in Australia. In Greek mythology, Ella (Ancient Greek: Ἕλλα) was the daughter of Athamas and Nephele.
results.Eva: Eva is a female given name derived from the Greek Εὕα (Heúa), and ultimately from the Hebrew חַוָּה (Ḥawwāh), the name of the first woman in the Book of Genesis. The name spread widely in Europe through the Latin Bible and remains common in many languages.
results.Fabian: Fabian is the English form of the late Roman name Fabianus. This was a name originally given to those adopted into or descended through the female line from a Roman family named Fabius, that derived from the Latin faba for the broad bean, an important food crop in antiquity.
results.Falk: Falk is a given name and surname cognate with the word falcon.
results.Florian: Florian is a masculine given name borrowed from the ancient Roman name Florianus. The name is derived from Florus, from Latin flōrus (originally "yellow, blond", later "flowering"), related to flāvus ("yellow, blond").
results.Gisela: Gisela is a female given name of Germanic origin. The name derives from the Old High German word gīsal, "pledge".
results.Gustav: Gustav, also spelled Gustaf (pronounced   or  in English; Swedish: [ˈɡɵ̂sːtav] for both spellings), is a male given name of Old Swedish origin, used mainly in Scandinavian countries, German-speaking countries, and the Low Countries.  The origin of the name is debated.
results.Heike: Heike is a given name of Germanic origin, most commonly but not exclusively female. The male form is Heiko.
results.Hermann: Hermann or Herrmann is the German origin of the given name Herman.
results.Jan:
Jan is a form of John that is used in various languages. )
The name is used in Afrikaans, Belarusian, Circassian, Catalan, Cornish, Croatian, Czech, English (especially in Devon dialect), Dutch, German, Kazakh, Polish, Slovak, Slovenian, Scandinavian and Finnic languages.
results.Jonas: Jonas is a common male name in many countries in the Western world and Northeast Africa. It is primarily used as a first name, but also occurs as a surname.
results.Karla: Karla is the feminine form of Karl.
results.Lara: Lara is a feminine given name or a surname in several languages. It can be used as a short form of the name Larissa.
results.Lena: Lena is a feminine given name, a short form of Helena (Ἑλενα), meaning 'torch' or 'shining light'. It may be a given name by itself or a diminutive of Helena and variants, such as Elena.
results.Lotta: Lotta is given name and nickname that is a diminutive of Charlotte and Charlotta.
results.Lotte: Lotte is a female given name. It is a diminutive of the names Lieselotte and Charlotte, which itself is a female form of the male name Charlot, a diminutive of Charles.
results.Maren:
Maren is a Germanic feminine given name that originated as a Danish variant of the name Marina.
Maren is also a surname.
results.Michelle: ". The usual Latin feminine form of the name was Michaela, with Michael the vernacular form for both men and women.
results.Moritz: Moritz is a given name and a surname. It is a German equivalent of the name Maurice.
results.Niklas: Niklas is a masculine given name, a Germanic variant of Nicholas. It is most common in Sweden and among the Swedish-speaking population of Finland.
results.Ole: Ole is a Danish and Norwegian masculine given name, derived from the Old Norse name Óláfr, meaning "ancestor's descendant".
results.Samuel: Samuel (Hebrew: שְׁמוּאֵל Šəmūʾēl, Tiberian: Šămūʾēl) is a male name and a surname of Hebrew origin. It means "name of God", deriving from the Hebrew Shem (שֵׁם) (which means "name") + ʾĒl (which means "God" or "deity").
results.Sebastian: Sebastian or Sebastiæn is both a given name and a surname.
results.Svea: Svea is a Swedish female name derived from the tribe called "Svear" or "Swedes," who came to conquer the land which is today's Sweden.  The name was very popular in Sweden during the first half of the 20th century, and in the 2010s began to revive in popularity.
results.Ursula: Ursula is a feminine given name in several  languages. The name is derived from a diminutive of the Latin ursa, which means "bear".
results.Vanessa: Vanessa is a feminine given name. It was created by the Anglo-Irish writer Jonathan Swift for Esther Vanhomrigh, whom Swift had met in 1708 and whom he tutored.
results.Volker: Volker is an old German name, derived from folk, folc (people, tribe), and heri (army, warrior). Which means people’s defender.
results.Werner: Werner is a name of German origin and is common both as a given name and a surname.
results.Xenia: Xenia (variants include Ksenia, Kseniia, Ksenija, Kseniya; derived from Greek Ξένια xenia, "hospitality") is a female given name. The below sections list notable people with one of the variants of this given name.
results.Aleyna: Aleyna is a feminine Turkish given name.
results.Alp: Alp is a Turkish masculine name meaning hero, brave, warrior. It has been used as a title, a given name, and a surname.
results.Aras: Aras is a masculine Lithuanian given name and surname. Rooted in old Lithuanian origins, the name Aras is associated with meanings such as "someone who takes responsibility" or "one who protects and cares deeply for what they value".
results.Arda: Arda is a given name of various origins. In Turkey, it is used as a masculine name.

results.Azra: Azra is a female given name. In Turkish, Azra means untouched.
results.Bahar: Bahar (Persian: بهار, lit. 'spring') in Persian appears as a feminine given name in Iran, Afghanistan, Pakistan, and Turkey.

results.Burak: Burak is a Turkish masculine name that derives from the Arabic Buraq, which literally means "lightning" and refers to a creature that transports prophets in Arabic tradition.

results.Çağlar: Çağlar is a Turkish masculine given name and surname that means "waterfall" or "lively".
results.Damla: Damla is a feminine Turkish name. In Turkish, "Damla" means "drop" (of water or rain).
results.Defne: Defne is a common feminine Turkish given name.

results.Doruk: Doruk is a Turkish given name and surname for males.
results.Efe: Efe is a masculine Turkish given name meaning 'brave' or 'valiant'. It was historically used as a title for respected men in Western Anatolia.
results.Ela:
Ela (or Elâ) is a feminine given name of Turkish origin meaning "hazel".
Ela is also an Aramaic feminine given name.
results.Elif: Elif (Turkish pronunciation: [elif]) is a name that is most commonly given to females in Turkey, but is also popular in other countries such as the Netherlands. In Greece, it is associated with the name Nefeli.
results.Emir: Emir is a male given name. It is derived from the Arabic title Emir or Amir.
results.Gul:
Gul  is a common name in Persian (گل Gol) and Turkish (Gül) languages, meaning rose. 
Gul is used as a family name in Europe, Central and South Asia.
results.Hazal: Hazal is a Turkish female given name that means dried tree leaves and autumn flower.

results.Kaan: Kaan is a masculine given name and surname of Turkish origin, meaning "ruler", "King of Kings" (alternatively spelled as Kağan, Khagan or Hakan, meaning "Khan of Khans").
results.Levent: Levent is a Turkish masculine given name, derived from Levend, and a surname.

Sultan (Arabic: سلطان) is a male given name and also a surname.

results.Fadi: It is common among Arab Christians but is also used among Muslims. Fady and Fadey are similar names.
results.Faisal: Faisal, Faisel, Faycal, Fayçal, Faysal, Faissal, Foysal, Fayssal, or Feisal (Arabic: فيصل) is a masculine given name of Arabic origin.
results.Ghada: Ghada (Arabic: غادة) is a feminine given name of Arabic origin  used predominantly in Arab countries, but also in non-Arab countries around the world. In Arabic, it refers to women who are attractive and graceful.
results.Hadi: Hadi or Hady (Arabic: هادي) is an Arabic masculine given name and surname, meaning "leader" or "guide". Al-Hadi ("The Guide") is one of the names of God in Islam.
results.Haitham: Haytham, Haitham or Haitem (Arabic: هيثم) is an Arabic male name meaning "young hawk" or "young eagle". It is highly popular among Middle Eastern communities and originated in Arab States of the Persian Gulf.
results.Hamdan: Hamdan (Arabic: حمدان Ḥamdān) is a name of Arab origin of aristocratic descent and many political ties within the middle east and the Arab World, controlling import/export mandates over port authorities.
results.Hamid: Hamid, Hamed, or Hameed is a masculine given name and surname of Arabic origin.
results.Harun: Harun (Arabic: هارون, Hārūn), also transliterated as Haroon, Hamroun, or Haroun, is a masculine given name and surname of Arabic origin, related to the Hebrew name of the Prophet Aaron. Both are most likely of Egyptian origin, from ꜥḥꜣ rw, meaning "warrior lion".
results.Hashem: HaShem (Hebrew: הַשֵּׁם, romanized: haššēm, lit. 'the name', often abbreviated to ה׳ [h′]) is a title used in Judaism to refer to God.
results.Haydar: Haydar (Arabic: حيدر), also spelt Hajdar, Hayder, Haidar, Heidar, Haider, Heydar, Hyder, and other variants, is an Arabic male given name, also used as a surname, and means an epithet for "lion".
results.Hisham: Hisham (Arabic: هشام) is an Arabic male given name which means "generous". It is not to be confused with the similar looking, but only slightly related, Hashim.
results.Hussein: Hussein, Hossein, Hussain, Hossain, Huseyn, Hüseyin, Husayn, Husein, Hussin, Hoessein, Houcine, Hocine or Husain (Arabic: حُسَيْن, romanized: Ḥusayn), coming from the triconsonantal root ḥ-s-n (ح س ن), is an Arabic name which is the diminutive of Hassan, meaning "good", "handsome" or "beautiful".
results.Ibtisam: Ibtisam Arabic: ابتسام, romanized: ibtisām is an Arabic ism "given name" meaning "smile". Among Arabic speakers, it is considered a woman's name, but among South Asian Muslims, it is also used as a male name.
results.Ilham: Ilham (إلهام) is a unisex name that derives from the Arabic word for inspiration. It is usually a given name, rarely used as a surname.
results.Imad: Emad (also transliterated as Imad, Imed and Aimad; Arabic: عماد) is an Arabic masculine given name and surname and means "support" or "pillar". What they trust.

results.Jamila: Jamila (Arabic: جميلة) is a feminine given name of Arabic origin. It is the feminine form of the masculine Arabic given name Jamil, which comes from the Arabic word jamāl (Arabic: جَمَال), meaning beautiful.
results.Jenan: Jenan (Persian: جنان, also Romanized as Jenān) is a village in Posht Tang Rural District, in the Central District of Sarpol-e Zahab County, Kermanshah Province, Iran. At the 2006 census, its population was 53, in 11 families.
results.Kareem: Kareem or Karim (Arabic: کریم) is a masculine given name and surname of Arabic origin that means "generous", "noble", or "honourable"; it is also one of the Names of God in Islam. The feminine form is Karima.
results.Khadija: Khadija, Khadijah, Khadeeja, Khatija, or Khatijah (Arabic: خديجة, romanized: Khadīja) is a feminine given name of Arabic origin. It is the name of Khadija bint Khuwaylid, the first wife of the Islamic prophet Muhammad.
results.Khalifa: Khalifa or Khalifah (Arabic: خليفة, romanized: Khalīfa; commonly "caliph" in English) is an Islamic title which literally means "successor" or "deputy of the God". It most commonly refers to the leader of a caliphate, but can also be used as a title among various Islamic religious groups and others.
results.Labib: Labib (Arabic: لبيب) is a masculine Arabic name.
results.Laith: Laith is a name that is an Arabic epithet for "lion". It also comes from a variant in Scottish from Leith, a placename element from Scottish Gaelic laith meaning "liquid", likely borrowed from Proto-Brythonic *lleɨθ "moist".
results.Lamia:
Lamia ( ; Ancient Greek: Λάμια, romanized: Lámia), in ancient Greek mythology, was a child-eating monster and, in later tradition, was regarded as a type of night-haunting spirit or "daimon".
In the earliest myths, Lamia was a beautiful queen of ancient Libya who had an affair with Zeus and gave birth to his children.
results.Lamya: Lamya Al-Mugheiry (30 October 1963 – 8 January 2009), better known as her mononym Lamya, was a Kenyan-born English singer-songwriter and record producer. results.Latifa: Latifa, Lateefa or Lateefah is a feminine Arabic (لٓطِيفٓة) given name which means "gentle", "nice" or "pleasant". It corresponds to the masculine Latif.
results.Layan: " Leen (Arabic: لين) is a related name. Both are among the most popular names given to newborn girls in the Arab world in the past decade.
results.Lina: Lina ( LEE-nə) is a feminine given name with many origins in different nations.
results.Luqman: Luqman (Arabic: لقمان, romanized: Luqmān; also known as Luqman al-Hakim, meaning Luqman the Wise) was a legendary sage and hero in pre-Islamic Arab tradition. results.Maimuna: Maimuna Amadu Murashko (née Diko; Belarusian: Маймуна Амаду Мурашка (Дзіка); Russian: Маймуна Амаду Мурашко (Дико); born 28 May 1980), known professionally as simply Maimuna, is a Belarusian violinist who represented Belarus in the Eurovision Song Contest 2015 along with Uzari with the song "Time".
results.Marwan: Marwan, Merwan or Marwen or Mervan (Arabic: مروان, romanized: Marwān) is an Arabic male given name derived from the word maruww (مرو) with the meaning of either minerals, 'flint(-stone)', 'quartz"' or 'hard stone of nearly pure silica'. results.Maymuna: Maymūna (ميمونة) is a female Arabic name. Variant spellings in English include: Maimoonah, Maymoonah, Maymuna(h), Maimouna, Mahmuna and Mehmoona, Maimuna, Mymouna(h), Mymona.
results.Menna: The ancient Egyptian official named Menna carried a number of titles associated with the agricultural estates of the temple of Karnak and the king.  Information about Menna comes primarily from his richly decorated tomb (TT 69) in the necropolis of Sheikh Abd al-Qurna at Thebes.
results.Mira: Mira (pronounced , MY-rə) is a binary star system in the constellation Cetus. It has the Bayer designation Omicron Ceti, which is Latinized from ο Ceti, and abbreviated Omicron Cet or ο Cet.
results.Murad: Murad or Mourad (Arabic: مراد) is an Arabic name. It is also common in Armenian, Azerbaijani, Bengali, Turkish, Persian, and Berber as a male given name or surname and is commonly used throughout the Muslim world and Middle East.
results.Mustafa: Mustafa (Arabic: مصطفى, romanized: Muṣṭafā) is one of the names of the Islamic prophet Muhammad. It is Arabic for "chosen, selected, appointed, preferred".
results.Nabil: Nabīl, Nabeel, or Nabyl (Arabic: نبيل), rendered in some languages as Nebil, is a masculine given name of Arabic origin, meaning "noble". The feminine version is Nabila, Nabilah, Nabeela or Nabeelah.
results.Nabila: Nabila, and its variant spellings Nabeela, Nabillah, Nebila,  and Nabeelah, is the feminine variation of the given name Nabil, meaning noble.
results.Nader: Nader is a masculine given name and surname of Arabic origin (نادر Nādir, meaning "rare", "unique"). The name Nadir is a variant.
results.Nadia: Nadia is a female name. Variations include Nadja, Nadya, Nadine, Nadiya, and Nadiia.
results.Nadira: Nadira, Nadirah, or Nodira is a feminine given name of Arabic origin.
results.Naima: "Naima" ( ny-EE-mə) is a jazz ballad composed by John Coltrane in 1959 that he named after his then-wife, Juanita Naima Grubbs. Coltrane first recorded it for his 1959 album Giant Steps, and it became one of his first well-known works.
results.Nasir: Nasir (Arabic: نصیر, romanized: Naseer) is a masculine given name, commonly found in Arabic, which can mean "helper" or "one who gives victory" (grammatically the Stem I masculine singular active participle of consonantal verb root n-ṣ-r).

results.Suleiman:

results.Sumayya: Sumayyah (Arabic: سُمَيَّة; c. 550–615) was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad and the mother of Ammar Ibn Yasir, a prominent companion of the prophet.
results.Talal:
Talal or Telal (Arabic: طلال, Ṭalāl) is an Arabic masculine given name and a surname.
The name's Proto-Semitic root is ṭ-l-l, meaning "dew".
results.Tariq: Tariq (Arabic: طارق) is an Arabic word and given name.

results.Wael: Wa'el, also spelt Wael, is an ancient Aramaic male given name. The first currently known usage of the name was found and translated at a site called Sumatar Harabesi.
results.Wafa: Wafa (Arabic: وفا, lit. 'trust', an acronym of وكالة الأنباء الفلسطينية, Wikalat al-Anba al-Filastiniya, 'Palestinian News Agency'), also referred to in English as the Palestine News Agency and the Palestinian News & Info Agency, is the official state-run news agency of the Palestinian National Authority (PNA).
results.Wahid: Wahid or Waheed is an Arabic masculine given name, meaning "One", "Absolute One". Its feminine form is Wahida.
results.Waleed: Waleed (Arabic: وليد) or al-Waleed (الولید), also spelled al-Walid, Walid, Oualid, or Velid, is an Arabic-language masculine given name meaning newborn child.
results.Yasser: Yasser (also spelled Yaser, Yaseer, Yasir, or Yassir; Arabic: ياسر, romanized: Yāsir) is an Arabic male name meaning "to be of ease" or "of wealth".
results.Yumna: Yumna is a feminine given name of Arabic origin.
results.Yusuf: Yusuf (Arabic: يوسف Yūsuf) is an Arabic male name meaning "increases" (in piety, power and influence). It is the Arabic equivalent of the Hebrew name Yosef and the English name Joseph.
results.Zaher: Zaher (Arabic: زاهر) is a given name and surname of Arabic origin.
results.Zahi: Zahi is a given name of Arabic origin.
results.Zaid: Zaid or Zayd (; Arabic: زيد) is an Arabic given name and surname.
results.Zaina: Zaina is an Arabic name which means beauty, adornment, joyful, good looking and happy. It can also be a surname but only in a non Islamic manner.
results.Zaki: Zaki (Arabic: زكي) is an Arabic male name and surname. Zaki is a Quranic name meaning "pure", "virtuous", or "intelligent".
results.Zaynab:
Zaynab (Arabic: زينب, [ˈzeːnæb, ˈziːnæb, ˈzajnab]), and variant spellings, is an Arabic female given name meaning 'a flower in the desert'.
Zainab bint Muhammad was a daughter of the Islamic prophet Muhammad, Zaynab bint Ali was a granddaughter, two of his wives were Zaynab bint Jahsh and Zaynab bint Khuzayma.
results.Ziyad: Ziad (; Arabic: زياد, romanized: Ziād) is an Arabic given name and surname.
results.Ainsley: Ainsley (also spelt Ainsleigh) is both a unisex given name and a surname and place name. It is derived from words meaning hermitage and clearing (Old English "anne" ("alone, solitary") or ānsetl ("hermitage") + lēah ("woodland, clearing")).
results.Alder: Alders are trees of the genus Alnus in the birch family Betulaceae. The genus includes about 35 species of monoecious trees and shrubs, a few reaching a large size, distributed throughout the north temperate zone with a few species extending into Central America, as well as the northern and southern Andes.
results.Arthur: Arthur is a masculine given name of uncertain etymology. Its popularity derives from it being the name of the legendary hero King Arthur.
results.Astrid: Astrid is a given name of Scandinavian origin, a modern form of the name Ástríðr. Derived from the Old Norse Ássfriðr, a compound name composed of the elements áss (a god) and fríðr (beautiful, fair).
results.Aubrey: Aubrey () is a unisex English name. It was common for men and women in the Middle Ages but then lost favour for a time before experiencing a resurgence of popularity for men in the 19th century.
results.Audrey: Audrey is a feminine given name. It is rarely a masculine given name.
results.Autumn: Autumn, also known as fall in North American English, is one of the four temperate seasons on Earth. Outside the tropics, autumn marks the transition from summer to winter, beginning in September (Northern Hemisphere) or March (Southern Hemisphere).
results.Bear: Bears are carnivoran mammals of the family Ursidae (). They are classified as caniforms within the suborder Caniformia.
results.Bella: Bella is a feminine given name. It is a diminutive or nickname form of names ending in -bella, including Izabella and Isabella.
results.Bianca: Bianca is a feminine given name. It means "white" and is an Italian cognate of Blanche.
results.Blair:
Blair is a Scots-English-language name of Scottish Gaelic origin.
The surname is derived from any of the numerous places in Scotland called Blair, derived from the Scottish Gaelic blàr, meaning "plain", "meadow" or "field", frequently a battlefield.
results.Blossom:
In botany, blossoms are the flowers of stone fruit trees (genus Prunus) and of some other plants with a similar appearance that flower profusely for a period of time in spring.
Colloquially, flowers of orange are referred to as such as well.
results.Cadence: In Western musical theory, a cadence (from Latin  cadentia 'a falling') is the end of a phrase in which the melody or harmony creates a sense of full or partial resolution, especially in music of the 16th century onwards.
results.Canyon: A canyon (from Spanish  cañón; archaic British English spelling: cañon), gorge or chasm, is a deep cleft between escarpments or cliffs resulting from weathering and the erosive activity of a river over geologic time scales.
results.Cecily: Cecily is a feminine given name. It is an English form of the Latin name Cecilia, which is derived from the Roman Caecili family.
results.Charles: Charles is a male given name predominantly found in English and French speaking countries. It is from the French form Charles of the Proto-Germanic name ᚲᚨᚱᛁᛚᚨᛉ (in runic alphabet) or *karilaz (in Latin alphabet), whose meaning was "free man".

results.Chloe: Chloe (; Greek: Χλόη), also spelled Chloë, Chlöe, or Chloé, is a feminine name meaning "blooming" or "fertility" in Greek. The name ultimately derives, through Greek, from the Proto-Indo-European root *ǵʰelh₃-, which relates to the colors yellow and green.

Bellis perennis, the common daisy, lawn daisy, or English daisy, a European species

results.Deborah: According to the Book of Judges, Deborah (Hebrew: דְּבוֹרָה, Dəḇōrā) was a prophetess of Judaism, the fourth Judge of pre-monarchic Israel and the only female judge mentioned in the Hebrew Bible.
results.Demi: Demi is a feminine given name with Greek and Latin roots, and it is a surname with Albanian origins. Demi was originally a nickname of Demetria, the feminine form of the masculine name Demetrius, which is itself the Latin and English spelling of the Greek name Demetrios.
results.Derek: Derek is a masculine given name. It is the English language short form of Diederik, the Low Franconian form of the name Theodoric.
results.Diana:
Diana most commonly refers to:

Diana (given name), given name (including a list of people with the name)
Diana (mythology), ancient Roman goddess of the hunt and wild animals; later associated with the Moon
Diana, Princess of Wales (1961–1997), formerly Lady Diana Spencer, activist, philanthropist, and member of the British royal family

results.Edith: Edith is a feminine given name derived from the Old English word ēad, meaning wealth or prosperity, in combination with the Old English gȳð, meaning strife, and is in common usage in this form in English, German, many Scandinavian languages and Dutch. Its French form is Édith.
results.Edmund: Edmund is a masculine given name in the English language. The name is derived from the Old English elements ēad, meaning "prosperity" or "riches", and mund, meaning "protector".
results.Edward: Edward is an English masculine name. It is derived from the Anglo-Saxon name Ēadweard, composed of the elements ēad "wealth, fortune; prosperity" and weard "guardian, protector”.
results.Edwin: The name Edwin means "wealth-friend". It comes from Old English: ēad (wealth, good fortune) and Old English: wine (friend).
results.Eleanor: Eleanor () is a feminine given name, originally from an Old French adaptation of the Old Provençal name Aliénor. It was the name of a number of women of royalty and nobility in western Europe during the High Middle Ages.
results.Ember: An ember, also called a hot coal, is a hot lump of smouldering solid fuel, typically glowing, composed of greatly heated wood, coal, or other carbon-based material. Embers (hot coals) can exist within, remain after, or sometimes precede, a fire.
results.Emily: Emily is a feminine given name derived from the Roman family name "Aemilius", and is the feminine form of the name Emil.
results.Eric: The male given names Eric, Erich, Erikk, Erik, Erick, Eirik, or Eiríkur are derived from the Old Norse name Eiríkr [ˈɛiˌriːkz̠] (or Eríkr [ˈeˌriːkz̠] in Old East Norse due to monophthongization).
results.Erin: Erin is a personal name taken from the Hiberno-English word for Ireland, originating from the Irish word "Éirinn".
results.Ernest: Ernest is a given name derived from the Germanic word ernst, meaning "serious", often shortened to Ernie.
results.Esther: Esther (; Hebrew: אֶסְתֵּר, romanized: ʾEstēr), originally Hadassah (; Hebrew: הֲדַסָּה, romanized: Hăḏassā), is the eponymous heroine of the Book of Esther in the Hebrew Bible.
results.Evan: Evan is a Welsh and English masculine given name, derived from Iefan, a Welsh form of the name John. Evan can also occasionally be found as a shortened version of Greek names like Evangelos, Evander, or Evandro.
results.Faith:
In religion, faith is the "belief in God or in the doctrines or teachings of religion".
Religious people often think of faith as confidence based on a perceived degree of warrant, or evidence, while others who are more skeptical of religion tend to think of faith as belief without evidence.
results.Finn: The word Finn (pl. Finns) usually refers to Finnish people, a Finnic ethnic group.
results.Flint: Flint, occasionally flintstone (SiO2), is a sedimentary cryptocrystalline form of the mineral quartz, categorized as the variety of chert that occurs in chalk or marly limestone. Historically, flint was widely used to make stone tools and start fires.
results.Flora: : floras or florae) is all the plant life present in a particular region or time, generally the naturally occurring (indigenous) native plants. The corresponding term for animals is fauna, and for fungi, it is funga.
results.Florence: Florence (Italian: Firenze) is the capital and most populous city of the Italian region of Tuscany, and, as of 2026, with a population of 361,625, the 8th most populous city in the country.
results.Fox: Foxes are small-to-medium-sized omnivorous mammals belonging to several genera of the family Canidae. They have a flattened skull; upright, triangular ears; a pointed, slightly upturned snout; and a long, bushy tail ("brush").
results.Frances: Frances is an English given name or last name of Latin origin. ' The male version of the name in English is Francis.
results.Gwendolyn: Gwendolyn is a feminine given name, a variant spelling of Gwendolen (perhaps influenced by names such as Carolyn, Evelyn and Marilyn). This has been the most popular spelling in the United States.
results.Hawthorne: Hawthorne often refers to the American writer Nathaniel Hawthorne.
results.Hazel: Hazels are plants of the genus Corylus of deciduous trees and large shrubs native to the temperate Northern Hemisphere. The genus is usually placed in the birch family, Betulaceae, though some botanists split the hazels (with the hornbeams and allied genera) into a separate family Corylaceae.
results.Heath: A heath () is a shrubland habitat found mainly on free-draining infertile, acidic soils and is characterised by open, low-growing woody vegetation. Moorland is generally related to high-ground heaths with—especially in Great Britain—a cooler and damper climate.
results.Hope: Hope is an optimistic state of mind that is based on an expectation of desirable outcomes with respect to events and circumstances in one's own life, or the world at large. As a verb, Merriam-Webster defines hope as "to expect with confidence" or "to cherish a desire with anticipation".

results.Jasper: Jasper is an opaque type of silica that comes in a variety of colors, most commonly red, yellow, brown, green, and very rarely blue. It is made mostly of very fine-grained quartz or chalcedony, with other minerals contributing to its color and appearance.
results.Juniper: Junipers are coniferous trees and shrubs in the genus Juniperus ( joo-NIP-ər-əs) of the cypress family Cupressaceae.
results.Kirkley: Kirkley is an area of the town of Lowestoft in the East Suffolk district of the English county of Suffolk. It is located south of the centre of Lowestoft and the town's harbour and Lake Lothing.
results.Landon: Landon is a personal name and surname of English origin that means "long hill". It is a variant of Langdon.
results.Lucy: Lucy was an English feminine given name derived from the Latin masculine given name Lucius with the meaning as of light (born at dawn or daylight, maybe also shiny, or of light complexion). Alternative spellings are Luci and Lucie.
results.Lynx: : lynx or lynxes) is any of the four extant species (the Canada lynx, Iberian lynx, Eurasian lynx and the bobcat) within the medium-sized wild cat genus Lynx.
results.Mabel: Mabel is an English female name derived from the Latin amabilis, "lovable, dear".
results.Maeve: Maeve, Meave, Maev or Maiv, Maiev ( mayv) is a female given name of Irish origin. It comes from the Irish name Méabh, which was spelt Meadhbh or Maedhbh in Early Modern Irish (pronounced [mʲɛɣβ]), Meḋḃ or Meaḋḃ in Middle Irish, and Medb in Old Irish (pronounced [mʲeðβ]).
results.Magnolia: Magnolia is a large genus of about 210 to 340 flowering plant species in the subfamily Magnolioideae of the family Magnoliaceae.
results.Martha: Martha (Aramaic: מָרְתָא‎) is a biblical figure described in the Gospels of Luke and John. Together with her siblings Lazarus and Mary of Bethany, she is described as living in the village of Bethany near Jerusalem and witnessing Jesus resurrecting her brother, Lazarus.
results.Melody: A melody (from Greek  μελῳδία (melōidía) 'singing, chanting'), also tune, voice, or line, is a linear succession of musical tones that the listener perceives as a single entity.
results.Nell: Nell is a traditional nickname for Eleanor.
results.Ollie: Ollie is a given name and a nickname, often as a shortened form of Oliver, Olive, Olympia, Olga, or Olivia. Variants include Olie, Oli, Oly, and Olly.
results.Petra: Petra (Arabic: ٱلْبَتْراء, romanized: al-Batrāʾ; Ancient Greek: Πέτρα, lit. 'Rock'), originally known to its inhabitants as Raqmu (Nabataean Aramaic: 𐢛𐢚𐢒‎ or 𐢛𐢚𐢓𐢈‎, *Raqēmō), is an ancient city and archaeological site in southern Jordan.
results.Philippa: Philippa is a feminine given name meaning "lover of horses" or "horses' friend", from the Greek Philippos, which is derived from philein, meaning to love and hippos, meaning horse. The English masculine form is Philip, which was formerly the vernacular form for both sexes.
results.Poppy: A poppy is a flowering plant in the subfamily Papaveroideae of the family Papaveraceae. Poppies are herbaceous plants, often grown for their colourful flowers.
results.Presley: Presley is a surname and given name.
results.Reggie: Reggie is a given name, usually a short form of Reginald (male) or Regina (female).
results.Ridge: A ridge is a long, narrow, elevated geomorphologic landform, structural feature, or a combination of both separated from the surrounding terrain by steep sides. The sides of a ridge slope away from a narrow top, the crest or ridgecrest, with the terrain dropping down on either side.
results.River: A river is a natural stream of fresh water that flows on land or inside caves towards another body of water at a lower elevation, such as an ocean, lake, or another river. A river may run dry before reaching the end of its course if it runs out of water, or only flow during certain seasons.
results.Ruby: Ruby is a pinkish-red to blood-red-colored gemstone, a variety of the mineral corundum, consisting of aluminium oxide (α-Al2O3). Ruby is one of the most popular traditional jewelry gems and is very durable.
results.Rufus: Rufus is a masculine given name, a surname, an Ancient Roman cognomen and a nickname (from Latin rufus, "red").
results.Sawyer: A sawyer (occupation) is someone who saws wood.
results.Tamsin: Tamsin is a short form of Thomasina.
results.Trinity: The Trinity (Latin: Trinitas, lit. 'triad', from trinus 'threefold') is a Christian doctrine concerning the nature of God.
results.Verity: ) is a female first name and a surname. As a first name it derives from the Latin feminine noun veritas, meaning "truth".

results.Virginia: Virginia, officially the Commonwealth of Virginia, is a state in the Southeastern and Mid-Atlantic regions of the United States between the Atlantic Coast and the Appalachian Mountains.
results.William: William is a masculine given name of Germanic origin. It became popular in England after the Norman conquest in 1066, and remained so throughout the Middle Ages and into the modern era.
results.Winter: Winter is the coldest and darkest season of the year in temperate and polar climates. It occurs after autumn and before spring, when the hemisphere is oriented away from the Sun as a result of the tilt of Earth's axis.
results.Alina: Alina is a feminine given name with multiple origins in different cultures. It might be a form of Aline, which originated as a shortened form of Adeline, meaning noble.
results.Andreas: Andreas (Greek: Ἀνδρέας) is a name derived from the Greek noun ἀνήρ anēr, with genitive ἀνδρός andros, which means "man". See the article on Andrew for more information.
results.Annika: Annika is a feminine given name with multiple origins in different cultures. It is a Swedish diminutive for Anna, derived in the 15th century from Anneke, a Dutch and Northern Germanic diminutive of Anna.
results.Antje: Antje  is a female name. It is a Low German and Dutch diminutive form of Anna.
results.Armin: Armin is a male given name and surname of Indo-European origin.
results.Bastian: Bastian is a German short form of Sebastian.
results.Benedikt: Benedikt is a spelling of the masculine given name Benedict.
results.Cecilia: Cecilia is a personal name originating in the name of Saint Cecilia, the patron saint of music.
results.Christoph: Christoph is a male given name and surname. It is a German variant of Christopher.
results.Clemens: Clemens is a Late Latin, German, and Dutch masculine given name and a surname, meaning "merciful".

results.Dieter: Dieter is a German given name, a short form of Dietrich, from  theod+ric "people ruler" (see Theodoric). Rarely, it is a German form of the given name Theodore.
results.Dietrich: Dietrich (German pronunciation: [ˈdiːtʁɪç] ) is an ancient Germanic dithematic name meaning "ruler of the people". It may be both a given name and a surname.
results.Dorothea: Dorothea, also spelt Dorothee (German), Dorothée (French), and Dorotea, is a female given name from Greek Δωροθέα (Dōrothéa) meaning "god's gift". In English it is more commonly spelt Dorothy.
results.Elias: Elias ( il-EYE-əs; Ancient Greek: Ἠλίας, romanized: Elías) is the hellenized version for the name of Elijah (Hebrew: אֵלִיָּהוּ, romanized: ʾĒlīyyāhū; Syriac: ܐܠܝܐ, romanized: Elyāe; Arabic: إلیاس, romanized: Ilyās, or إلیا, Ilyā), a prophet in the Northern Kingdom of Israel in the 9th century BC, mentioned in several holy books.
results.Elke: Elke (see panel for pronunciation) is a feminine given name. Different sources give different accounts of its origin.
results.Emmeline: Emmeline, The Orphan of the Castle is the first novel written by English writer Charlotte Smith; it was published in 1788. A Cinderella story in which the heroine stands outside the traditional economic structures of English society and ends up wealthy and happy, the novel is a fantasy.
results.Ernst: Ernst  is both a surname and a given name, the German, Dutch, and Scandinavian form of Ernest.
results.Ferdinand: Ferdinand is a Germanic name composed of  the  elements farð 'journey, travel', Proto-Germanic *farthi, abstract noun from root *far- 'to fare, travel' (PIE *par 'to lead, pass over'), and nanth 'courage' or  nand 'ready, prepared' related to Old High German nendan 'to risk, venture'.
results.Frauke: Frauke is a feminine German given name.
results.Fritz: Fritz is a common German male given name and also a surname.
results.Genoveva: Genoveva, Op. 81, is an opera in four acts by Robert Schumann in the genre of German Romanticism with a libretto by Robert Reinick and the composer.
results.Gunther: Gundaharius or Gundahar or Gunther (Middle High German: Gunther), was a historical King of the Burgundians in the early 5th century. Gundahar is attested as ruling his people shortly after they crossed the Rhine into Roman Gaul.
results.Heidi: Heidi ( HY-dee, German: [ˈhaɪdi]) is a work of children's fiction published between 1880 and 1881 by Swiss author Johanna Spyri, originally published in two parts as Heidi: Her Years of Wandering and Learning (German: Heidis Lehr- und Wanderjahre) and Heidi: How She Used What She Learned (German: Heidi kann brauchen, was es gelernt hat) by the publishing house Friedrich Andreas Perthes of Gotha.
results.Heidrun: Heidrun or Heiðrún is a female name originally from Norse mythology.
results.Helga: Helga (from Old Norse  heilagr 'holy, blessed') is a female name, used mainly in Scandinavia, German-speaking countries and the Low Countries (Hege, Helle, Helge, Helga, Helka or Oili). The name was in use in England before the Norman Conquest, but appears to have died out afterwards.
results.Henrik: Henrik is a male given name of Germanic origin, primarily used in Scandinavia, Finland, Estonia, Hungary and Slovenia. In Poland, the name is spelt Henryk but pronounced similarly.
results.Henrike: Henrike is a feminine given name of Germanic origin, the female form of the male given name Henrik.
results.Inge: Inge is a given name in various Germanic language-speaking cultures. In Swedish and Norwegian, it is mostly used as a masculine, but less often also as a feminine name.
results.Ingeborg: Ingeborg is a Germanic feminine given name, mostly used in Germany, Denmark, Sweden and Norway, derived from Old Norse Ingiborg, Ingibjǫrg, combining the theonym Ing with the element borg "stronghold, protection". Ingebjørg is the Norwegian most used variant of the name, and Ingibjörg is the Icelandic variant.
results.Janosch: Janosch (German: [ˈjaːnɔʃ] , born as Horst Eckert on 11 March 1931) is a German children's author and illustrator.
results.Jesper: Jesper is a given name commonly believed to be of ancient Persian origin, meaning "Treasurer".
results.Joachim: Joachim was, according to Christian Sacred tradition, the husband of Saint Anne, the father of Mary and grandfather of Jesus. The story of Joachim and Anne first appears in the Gospel of James, part of the New Testament apocrypha.
results.Johann: Johann (German pronunciation: [ˈjoːhan] ) is a German male given name.
results.Johanna: Johanna is a feminine name, a variant form of Joanna that originated in Latin in the Middle Ages, including an -h- by analogy with the Latin masculine name Johannes. The original Greek form Iōanna lacks a medial /h/ because in Greek /h/ could only occur initially.
results.Katharina: Katharina is a feminine given name. It is a German form of Katherine.
results.Kathrin: Kathrin or Katrin or Kathryn or Kathrine is a female given name.
results.Kerstin: Kerstin is a female German and Swedish given name; it is the European version of Christina.
results.Klaus: Klaus is a German, Dutch, Scandinavian, and Greek given name and surname. It originated as a short form of Nikolaus, a German form of the Greek given name Nicholas.
results.Konstantin: Konstantin (Cyrillic: Константин) is a given name and sometimes a surname. It is used in some European languages, such as Bulgarian, Russian, Estonian, and German.
results.Kristina: Kristina is a feminine given name and a variant of Christina.
results.Kunigunde: Kunigunde, Kunigunda, or Cunigunde, is a European female name of German origin. It consists of two Old High German roots kunni ('clan', 'family') + gunda ('fight').
results.Lasse: Lasse is a common masculine given name in Nordic countries. It is also often a nickname for people named Lars or Lauri.
results.Laurenz: Laurenz can be a masculine given name, a middle name, or a surname.
results.Leoni: Leoni is an Italian surname, literally meaning "lions".
results.Liesel: The name Liesel is short for Elizabeth. The name was most popular during the 17th century.
results.Lieselotte: Lieselotte is a German feminine given name. It is derived from a combination of the names Lise, a diminutive form of Elisabeth, and Lotte, a diminutive of  Charlotte.
results.Liesl: Liesl is a feminine given name of German origin. It is a diminutive of Lieselotte and Elisabeth.
results.Linus: Linus, a male given name, is the Latin form of the Greek name Linos. It is a common given name in Sweden.
results.Livia:
Livia Drusilla (30 January 59 BC – 
AD 29) was Roman empress from 27 BC to AD 14 as the wife of Augustus, the first Roman emperor. She was known as Julia Augusta after her formal adoption into the Julia gens in AD 14.
results.Lorenz: Lorenz is an originally German name derived from the Roman surname Laurentius, which means "from Laurentum".
results.Lukas: Lukas is a  form of the Greek name Λουκάς, which can be alternatively Romanized as Loukas, Luke, or Lucas.
results.Magnus: Magnus, meaning "great" in Latin, was used as cognomen in ancient Rome and a given name in the Middle Ages.
results.Margarete: Margarete is a German feminine given name. It is derived from Ancient Greek margarites (μαργαρίτης), meaning "the pearl".
results.Marieke: Marieke (Dutch pronunciation: [maːˈrikə] ), also spelled Marike, is a Dutch-language feminine given name, a diminutive of Maria. The Polish, Greek and Japanese equivalent is Marika.
results.Matteo: Matteo is the Italian form of the given name Matthew. Another form is Mattia.
results.Matthias: Matthias is a name derived from the Greek Ματθαίος, in origin similar to Matthew.
results.Maximilian:
Maximilian or Maximillian (Maximiliaan in Dutch and Maximilien in French) is a male name.
